equations.defuzzified: raw(x) = sum_r w_r(x) f_r(x) / sum_r w_r(x)

files.membership_curves.csv: Gaussian membership values on a dense x grid, with centres and widths.
files.rule_summary.csv: Learned consequents plus mean/max normalised rule firing and contribution by split.
files.rule_activations.csv: Per-forecast normalised firing and contribution for every rule.
files.forecast_effects.csv: Per-forecast inputs, m, exp(m), s, base/adjusted quantiles, component deltas, coverage and pinball losses.
files.effect_summary.csv: Pooled and per-class summaries of layer behaviour.
files.partial_dependence.csv: One-input-at-a-time partial dependence over observed standardised inputs.
files.response_surfaces.csv: Two-input FIS response on a standardised grid (h=1 and h=7, width and location).

forecast_effects.m: Width FIS output: log multiplier on both half-widths.
forecast_effects.width_multiplier: exp(m); values below one narrow the interval, above one widen it.
forecast_effects.s: Location FIS output added to P50; P10 and P90 move with it.
forecast_effects.s_relative: s divided by the horizon's bounded location scale.
forecast_effects.width_only_delta_*: Quantile change from the width system alone.
forecast_effects.loc_only_delta_*: Quantile change from the location system alone.
forecast_effects.*_z: Standardised FIS inputs actually seen by the membership functions.

rule_summary.antecedents: Input membership indices in the learned rule order.
rule_summary.consequent: Constant rule output before weighting and tanh.
rule_summary.activation_mean: Mean normalised rule firing; all rules sum to one per forecast.
rule_summary.contribution_mean: Mean weighted rule contribution to the raw FIS output.

notes: The width FIS uses cov_gap and vol_z at h=1 and h=7, and vol_z only at h=30 and h=90.
The location FIS uses bias_z and vol_z at every horizon.
Within-interval movement comes from s; exp(m) scales the lower and upper half-widths around the shifted median.
Rule activation is normalised by the sum of all rule weights for that forecast.
